title: Egyptian and Nigerian English join the Open ASR Leaderboard
gist: Hugging Face's Open ASR Leaderboard adds two private held-out splits (Egyptian and Nigerian conversational English, ~1.3-1.6h each) from Liva AI, continuing a push toward private eval data to counter benchmark gaming and broaden accent coverage. The leaderboard now reports accent breakdowns using Kachru's Three Circles (US vs non-US; Inner vs Outer & Expanding Circles).

insights.claim: Hugging Face's Open ASR Leaderboard is increasingly relying on private, held-out evaluation data to minimize benchmark overfitting ('benchmaxxing') and improve trust in speech-recognition rankings.
insights.speaker: Eric Bezzam
insights.so_what: Public ASR benchmark scores are losing credibility; vendors that rank well on private sets gain a more defensible marketing claim.
insights.quote: to improve trust (new private data to minimize benchmaxxing, and new data providers)
insights.locator: This is part of our continued

insights.claim: The Open ASR Leaderboard's private data has grown from 11 splits from Appen and DataOceanAI covering five accents, to an added Indian-accented split from Voice Arena, and now two Liva AI splits for Egyptian and Nigerian English.
insights.speaker: Eric Bezzam
insights.so_what: Evaluation-data suppliers (Appen, DataOceanAI, Liva AI) are becoming part of the AI benchmark supply chain, a niche demand driver for data vendors.
insights.locator: A few months ago, we added

insights.claim: The new Liva AI splits are small: 1.34 hours of Egyptian and 1.55 hours of Nigerian conversational, spontaneous English, transcribed with punctuation, casing and disfluencies.
insights.speaker: Eric Bezzam
insights.so_what: Low hour counts mean per-accent results may be noisy; investors should treat small rank differences on these splits cautiously.

themes.theme: Accent coverage via Kachru's Three Circles

insights.claim: The Open ASR Leaderboard now reports accent performance as US vs non-US (UK, Australia, Canada, India, Nigeria, Egypt) and Inner Circle (US, UK, Australia, Canada) vs Outer & Expanding Circles (India, Nigeria, Egypt), an idea credited to Hume AI's leaderboard.
insights.speaker: Eric Bezzam
insights.so_what: Explicit non-US / Global South accent metrics will expose ASR models that underperform outside Anglo markets, relevant for vendors selling into emerging markets.
insights.locator: Richer accent breakdown in the Private tab

insights.claim: Hugging Face plans to further split the Outer and Expanding Circles categories as more accents are added, signalling continued expansion of non-Western accent and language coverage in ASR evaluation.
insights.speaker: Eric Bezzam
insights.so_what: Growing granular evaluation of emerging-market speech raises the bar for ASR products targeting Africa, the Middle East and South Asia.
insights.quote: As more accents join, we’ll split the Outer and Expanding Circles.

insights.claim: Liva AI collects multimodal interaction data through its own consumer products, and because it owns both the collection environment and distribution, it can design products around specific model gaps across domains, languages, modalities and interaction types.
insights.speaker: Eric Bezzam
insights.so_what: A vertically integrated 'consumer app as data engine' model is an emerging alternative to crowdsourced/annotation-vendor data, potentially with better moats.
insights.quote: Because Liva owns both the collection environment and distribution, it can design products around specific model gaps

insights.claim: Liva AI positions natural, high-context behavior from real product use as more valuable training and eval data than artificially elicited or task-based interactions.
insights.speaker: Eric Bezzam
insights.so_what: Demand is shifting toward naturalistic, spontaneous speech data, favoring data suppliers with real user distribution over scripted-recording vendors.
insights.quote: rather than artificially elicited or task-based interactions
